# European GPU price report: October 2026

Published 7 October 2026, rebuilt 29 October 2026. EUR list prices from 6 GPU providers with named EU or EEA sites: 26 price points for H100, H200, B200 and B300, each with site, source and date.

...

What is in this issue: public list prices in EUR, only where the provider's own pages place the GPU at a named site or region in the EU or EEA. Every row shows that site. USD lists are converted at the ECB euro reference rate of 1.1133 USD per EUR (28 October 2026).

In short: H100 on-demand at named EU or EEA sites listed from €2.34 (Taiga Cloud) to €4.26 (Verda) per GPU-hour, median €3.19. List prices are a starting point; term, minimum commitment, storage, egress and VAT change the bill.

## Highlights

1. H100 on-demand ran from €2.34 (Taiga Cloud, Sines, Portugal; Boden, Sweden; Kristiansand, Norway) to €4.26 (Verda) per GPU-hour across 6 providers. The median was €3.19. (Provider price lists, accessed 29 October 2026)
2. H200 on-demand: €3.85 at Crusoe (Iceland) to €5.56 at Verda, median €5.05 across 4 providers. (Provider price lists, accessed 29 October 2026)
3. B200 with a named EU site is rare: only Verda (Helsinki, Finland) lists it, at €7.89 per GPU-hour on-demand. B300 is listed by 4 providers, from €7.50 (Scaleway, Paris, France). (Provider price lists, accessed 29 October 2026)
4. Commitment lowers the rate. Verda's published discounts take H100 from €4.26 on-demand to €3.92 on a 1-year term and €3.20 on a 2-year term. (Verda public price list, accessed 29 October 2026)
5. USD lists are converted at the ECB reference rate of 1.1133 USD per EUR of 28 October 2026. Quotes through Kraftcompute come from providers directly and depend on term, cluster size and site. (ECB euro reference rate, 28 October 2026)

results.title: Three European GPU clouds raised their prices for October, while AWS, Azure and Google Cloud held theirs. | Lindstead
results.author: Lindstead
highlights:
# Three European GPU clouds raised their prices for October, while AWS, Azure and Google Cloud held theirs. | Lindstead · LinkedIn · 2026-10-22T00:00:00+00:00

**Lindstead**.

---

Three European GPU clouds raised their prices for October, while AWS, Azure and Google Cloud held theirs.

On-demand price of one H100 per hour, September to October:
• Nebius (NL): €3.38 to €3.95, up 17%
• Scaleway (FR): €2.73 to €2.87, up 5%
• Verda (FI): €3.09 to €3.18, up 3%

Nebius raised its newest GPUs most. A B300 now costs €8.33 an hour, up 21 percent. OVHcloud and Hetzner did not change their prices.

MSP Business and Dutch IT Channel reported the Nebius increase on 30 September, citing the index.

results.title: Scaleway Review 2026: What the European Cloud Costs After the June Price Rise | The Proof Desk
results.author: The Proof Desk Team
highlights:
On 1 June 2026 Scaleway raised prices for the first time in three years. It blamed rising RAM and storage hardware costs and the global IPv4 shortage. The smallest instance now costs four times what it did, every flexible IPv4 address went up 25%, and GPUs rose by roughly 5-10%. Over the same months Dedibox and Elastic Metal got cheaper, B300 GPUs arrived and Milan opened, so the picture is mixed rather than simply worse.

...

- Best for: EU-based startups, AI teams that want per-minute H100 billing in Europe, and anyone who needs data kept out of US jurisdiction.
- Watch out for: IPv4 and block storage billed on top of every instance, low quotas until you verify your identity, paid support for fast responses, and no hard spending cap.
- Prices in this review are in euros excluding VAT, taken from Scaleway's pricing pages on 3 October 2026.

## What changed in the June 2026 price increase

Scaleway announced the rise in an April 2026 blog post titled "A transparent update on Scaleway pricing". It says the company had "proudly held our prices flat" for three years, and that anything not on its list keeps its old price. These are the changes most customers will notice:

- STARDUST1-S: €0.00015 to €0.0006 an hour (4x, roughly €0.11 to €0.44 a month).
- DEV1-S: €0.0088 to €0.00898 an hour; DEV1-M €0.0198 to €0.0202; DEV1-L €0.042 to €0.04284.
- PLAY2-PICO: €0.014 to €0.01428; PRO2-XXS: €0.055 to €0.0561 an hour.
- Flexible IPv4: €0.004 to €0.005 an hour. The same increase applies to Bare Metal, Public Gateway and Load Balancer IPs.
- H100-1-80G: €2.73 to €2.87 an hour; H100-SXM-8-80G: €23.03 to €25.33; L40S-1-48G: €1.40 to €1.47; L4-1-24G: €0.75 to €0.79.
- Block Storage SSD: €0.000118 to €0.00013 per GB per hour; Object Storage Multi-AZ: €0.00002 to €0.000022.
- Load Balancer GP-S: €0.016 to €0.023 an hour; Public Gateway S: €0.0199 to €0.026; DNS zone for external domains: €0.001 to €0.007.
- Serverless Functions: €0.000012 to €0.000017 per GB-second.
- Elastic Metal EM-I220E-NVMe: €199.99 to €229.99 a month; Dedibox Core-10-XS: €119.99 to €134.99.

...

- CPU instances are billed per hour of uptime, including startup and standby time. Each resource has a 60-minute minimum.
- GPU instances are billed per minute, except RENDER-S, which is billed per hour.
- Public IPs and volumes are billed for the whole time they are allocated, "regardless of whether the Instance is powered off." Powering off does not make a server free. You have to delete the IP and the volumes.
- Savings Plans promise up to 25% off compute if you commit to a monthly spend.

...

Elastic Metal can be rented by the hour, which suits short benchmarks or bursty batch jobs better than a classic dedicated server.

## GPUs and Generative APIs

Scaleway is one of the few EU-owned providers that sells H100 and B300 capacity on demand, billed per minute:

- L4-1-24G: €0.79/h (about €575/month), in PAR-1, PAR-2 and WAW-2.
- L40S-1-48G: about €1.47/h.
- H100-1-80G: about €2.87/h; H100-2-80G about €5.73/h.
- H100-SXM-8-80G: about €25.33/h (about €18,491/month).
- B300-SXM-8-288G: €60.00/h, PAR-2 only.
- No H200 or B200 instances are listed.

Generative APIs is the serverless model hosting service. It is priced per million tokens (input/output): gpt-oss-120b at €0.15/€0.60, Mistral Small 3.2 at €0.15/€0.35, Llama 3.3 70B at €0.90/€0.90, Qwen3 235B at €0.75/€2.25 and Mistral Medium 3.5 at €1.50/€7.50. Whisper transcription costs €0.003 per audio minute. New accounts get 1 million free tokens and 60 minutes of transcription, and the Batch API halves the price.

Two cautions apply. Dedicated Deployment (formerly Managed Inference) costs more than renting the same GPU yourself, for example €3.40 an hour for an H100 against about €2.87. And Scaleway retires serverless models fairly quickly: several, including Devstral 2, Pixtral and Qwen 3 Coder, were marked for end of life in July 2026. Pin model names and plan for migrations.

...

### How are Scaleway GPU instances billed?

Per minute of uptime, except RENDER-S, which is billed per hour. An H100-1-80G costs about €2.87 an hour and an eight-GPU H100 SXM node about €25.33. Stop and delete the instance when a job ends, because attached IPs and volumes keep billing.

results.title: 7 best ways to self-host AI inference on cloud GPUs in 2026 (GCP A5X, AWS and Scaleway compared) - Qovery Blog
results.author: Romaric Philogene
highlights:
- Renting an A5X-class GPU is the small part of the job. The bigger part is the GPU node pool, NVIDIA drivers and device plugin, an inference server (vLLM, SGLang or NVIDIA Dynamo/Triton), model weight storage and cold starts, GPU-aware

...

- The three clouds win on different axes. Google Cloud gets the newest NVIDIA silicon first (A5X on Vera Rubin NVL72, GA announced for November 2026). AWS has the deepest discount machinery (Savings Plans up to 72%, Spot up to 90%, Capacity Blocks for ML). Scaleway lists the cheapest H100 hour of the three, at €2.87 in Paris and Warsaw.
- Idle GPUs in dev and staging are the most avoidable line on an inference bill. A GPU node used 40 hours a week but left running all 168 hours spends about 76% of its time producing nothing.
- If you want self-hosted economics without hiring a platform team, run the inference service on Kubernetes inside your own AWS, GCP, Azure or Scaleway account (or your existing cluster) with an internal developer platform such as Qovery. The GPU bill, the committed-use discounts and the prompt data stay in your account.

...

On published on-demand list prices, Scaleway has the cheapest H100 hour of the three, AWS has the deepest discount machinery, and Google Cloud is where the newest NVIDIA generation lands first. Google Cloud's list prices look expensive, but its committed-use and Flex-start prices change the ranking.

results.title: GPU Instance Pricing in 2026: How to Compare AWS, GCP, Azure, and Scaleway Before You Commit - Qovery Blog
results.author: Romaric Philogene
highlights: The H100 tier. A full 8x H100 node runs $55.04/hour on AWS p5.48xlarge in us-east-1 (that is $6.88 per GPU-hour, SXM with NVLink) and $98.32/hour on an Azure ND H100 v5 node in East US (about $12.29 per GPU-hour, also SXM). Scaleway sells the H100 differently, per card: €2.73/hour for a single H100 PCIe 80GB. That PCIe-vs-SXM difference matters for multi-GPU training, which is exactly why you confirm the interconnect before you compare. Google's A3 (8x H100) price is published on the GCP GPU pricing page, but that table renders through a client-side calculator, so I am not going to quote a number I could not read straight from Google. Pull it live in the console or via the Billing Catalog API.

The GPU variant matters too. Scaleway lists a 1-GPU H100 PCIe instance at €2.87 per GPU-hour and an 8-GPU H100 SXM instance at €3.17 per GPU-hour. These are different products: SXM servers have the fast GPU-to-GPU links that multi-GPU training needs. Compare like for like.
